From 99c8c16a4aad0b37293cae213e15957c573cf79b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Bastien Curutchet (Schneider Electric)" <bastien.curutchet@bootlin.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 14:15:43 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] net: dsa: microchip: Fix error path in PTP IRQ setup

If request_threaded_irq() fails during the PTP message IRQ setup, the
newly created IRQ mapping is never disposed. Indeed, the
ksz_ptp_irq_setup()'s error path only frees the mappings that were
successfully set up.

Dispose the newly created mapping if the associated
request_threaded_irq() fails at setup.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: d0b8fec8ae505 ("net: dsa: microchip: Fix symetry in ksz_ptp_msg_irq_{setup/free}()")
Signed-off-by: Bastien Curutchet (Schneider Electric) <bastien.curutchet@bootlin.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Vladimir Oltean <olteanv@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260309-ksz-ptp-irq-fix-v1-1-757b3b985955@bootlin.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/dsa/microchip/ksz_ptp.c b/drivers/net/dsa/microchip/ksz_ptp.c
index 4a2cc57a628f..8b98039320ad 100644
--- a/drivers/net/dsa/microchip/ksz_ptp.c
+++ b/drivers/net/dsa/microchip/ksz_ptp.c
@@ -1108,6 +1108,7 @@ static int ksz_ptp_msg_irq_setup(struct ksz_port *port, u8 n)
 	const struct ksz_dev_ops *ops = port->ksz_dev->dev_ops;
 	struct ksz_irq *ptpirq = &port->ptpirq;
 	struct ksz_ptp_irq *ptpmsg_irq;
+	int ret;
 
 	ptpmsg_irq = &port->ptpmsg_irq[n];
 	ptpmsg_irq->num = irq_create_mapping(ptpirq->domain, n);
@@ -1119,9 +1120,13 @@ static int ksz_ptp_msg_irq_setup(struct ksz_port *port, u8 n)
 
 	strscpy(ptpmsg_irq->name, name[n]);
 
-	return request_threaded_irq(ptpmsg_irq->num, NULL,
-				    ksz_ptp_msg_thread_fn, IRQF_ONESHOT,
-				    ptpmsg_irq->name, ptpmsg_irq);
+	ret = request_threaded_irq(ptpmsg_irq->num, NULL,
+				   ksz_ptp_msg_thread_fn, IRQF_ONESHOT,
+				   ptpmsg_irq->name, ptpmsg_irq);
+	if (ret)
+		irq_dispose_mapping(ptpmsg_irq->num);
+
+	return ret;
 }
 
 int ksz_ptp_irq_setup(struct dsa_switch *ds, u8 p)
-- 
2.34.1

### Modifications in each file

- **File:** `drivers/net/dsa/microchip/ksz_ptp.c`
  - **Function changed:** `ksz_ptp_msg_irq_setup`
  - **Change:** Added a local variable `int ret` to capture the return value of `request_threaded_irq()`. Upon failure (non-zero return), the newly created IRQ mapping (obtained via `irq_create_mapping`) is now properly disposed of using `irq_dispose_mapping()` before returning the error. Previously, a failed `request_threaded_irq()` would leak the mapping.

### Relationship between modifications

The only modification is in a single file (`ksz_ptp.c`). It fixes a resource leak within the PTP message interrupt setup function by ensuring that an IRQ mapping created earlier is cleaned up if the subsequent IRQ request fails. This is a self-contained change that corrects the existing error path to align with the symmetric cleanup in `ksz_ptp_msg_irq_free()`.

Here is the commit message:
net: dsa: microchip: Fix error path in PTP IRQ setup

If request_threaded_irq() fails during the PTP message IRQ setup, the
newly created IRQ mapping is never disposed. Indeed, the
ksz_ptp_irq_setup()'s error path only frees the mappings that were
successfully set up.

Dispose the newly created mapping if the associated
request_threaded_irq() fails at setup.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: d0b8fec8ae505 ("net: dsa: microchip: Fix symetry in ksz_ptp_msg_irq_{setup/free}()")
Signed-off-by: Bastien Curutchet (Schneider Electric) <bastien.curutchet@bootlin.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Vladimir Oltean <olteanv@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260309-ksz-ptp-irq-fix-v1-1-757b3b985955@bootlin.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
When `request_threaded_irq()` fails in `ksz_ptp_msg_irq_setup()`, the IRQ mapping created by `irq_create_mapping()` earlier in the function is not disposed, leading to a resource leak. The error path only cleaned up previously successfully set up mappings (in the loop caller), but not the mapping just created for the current `n` value. This was introduced when the function was refactored in commit d0b8fec8ae505, which added the mapping creation but missed the corresponding cleanup on failure.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int ksz_ptp_msg_irq_setup(struct ksz_port *port, u8 n)
 {
 	u16 ts_reg[] = {REG_PTP_PORT_PDRESP_TS, REG_PTP_PORT_XDELAY_TS,
 			REG_PTP_PORT_SYNC_TS};
 	static const char * const name[] = {"pdresp-msg", "xdreq-msg",
 					    "sync-msg"};
 	const struct ksz_dev_ops *ops = port->ksz_dev->dev_ops;
 	struct ksz_irq *ptpirq = &port->ptpirq;
 	struct ksz_ptp_irq *ptpmsg_irq;
+	int ret;
 
 	ptpmsg_irq = &port->ptpmsg_irq[n];
 	ptpmsg_irq->num = irq_create_mapping(ptpirq->domain, n);
 	if (!ptpmsg_irq->num)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	ptpmsg_irq->port = port;
 	ptpmsg_irq->ts_reg = ops->get_port_addr(port->num, ts_reg[n]);
 
 	strscpy(ptpmsg_irq->name, name[n]);
 
-	return request_threaded_irq(ptpmsg_irq->num, NULL,
-				    ksz_ptp_msg_thread_fn, IRQF_ONESHOT,
-				    ptpmsg_irq->name, ptpmsg_irq);
+	ret = request_threaded_irq(ptpmsg_irq->num, NULL,
+				   ksz_ptp_msg_thread_fn, IRQF_ONESHOT,
+				   ptpmsg_irq->name, ptpmsg_irq);
+	if (ret)
+		irq_dispose_mapping(ptpmsg_irq->num);
+
+	return ret;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
ptpmsg_irq->num = irq_create_mapping(ptpirq->domain, n);
...
return request_threaded_irq(ptpmsg_irq->num, NULL,
			    ksz_ptp_msg_thread_fn, IRQF_ONESHOT,
			    ptpmsg_irq->name, ptpmsg_irq);
```
Reason:
When `irq_create_mapping()` succeeds but `request_threaded_irq()` fails, the newly created IRQ mapping is never disposed because the function returns directly without calling `irq_dispose_mapping()`. This causes a resource leak.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
+	int ret;
...
+	ret = request_threaded_irq(ptpmsg_irq->num, NULL,
+				   ksz_ptp_msg_thread_fn, IRQF_ONESHOT,
+				   ptpmsg_irq->name, ptpmsg_irq);
+	if (ret)
+		irq_dispose_mapping(ptpmsg_irq->num);
+
+	return ret;
```
Reason:
By saving the return value of `request_threaded_irq()` into a variable and adding a check, the fix ensures that when the request fails, the IRQ mapping is properly disposed via `irq_dispose_mapping()` before returning the error. This prevents the resource leak.
